text:
Repo topology & architectural layers:
- Roots: `atdd-bun.yaml` `topology:` keys `plan_root`, `source_root`, `test_root`, `e2e_root` (defaults `plan`, `src/wagons`, `tests/wagons`, `e2e`).
- Five fixed layers: domain, application, integration, presentation, assembly. Vocabulary is owned by core; adding a layer is a core change.
- A layer is identified by a path segment (domain/, application/, presentation/, integration/, assembly/). A file with no layer segment is outside layer rules, not in violation.
- domain/application/presentation are consumer (core) layers and depend only on neutral ports.
- integration/ (plus infrastructure/ dirs) is the outer ring: transport adapters, the centralized HTTP client, and adapters wiring external SDKs to ports.
- Unlayered entrypoints (composition root, scripts) wire adapters.
- Detector scope: test files and vendored/build dirs are never scanned; bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
- Component placement: frontend → presentation/application; backend → application/domain/integration; shared → cross-cutting.

coverage.note: path-segment bullet, consumer-layers bullet, integration/outer-ring bullet (centralized HTTP client)
layer list, ports bullet, outer-ring bullet (infrastructure/, SDK adapters), unlayered-entrypoints bullet
allowed-layer list in 'Five fixed layers' bullet; per-layer profile moved to notGeneric

notGeneric.content: Per-layer profile — presentation: methods render/handleInput/updateDisplay, consumes user interactions & display updates, produces ui events & user actions; application: methods execute/coordinate/validate, consumes commands & queries, produces events & responses; domain: methods process/calculate/applyRules, consumes domain events, produces domain events & state changes; integration: methods fetch/save/publish, consumes external events, produces external calls & persistence operations; assembly: no profile in source.

variants.note: Roots bullet preserves the configuration file, all four topology keys, and their defaults.
Path-segment, consumer-layer, and outer-ring bullets preserve layer identification, transport adapters, centralized HTTP client placement, and exclusion of unlayered files.
Detector scope and no-layer-segment clause preserve all scan exclusions, npm resolution outside the project graph, and treatment of unlayered files.
Five fixed layers bullet preserves the complete vocabulary and core ownership of additions.
Detector scope bullet preserves test and vendored/build exclusions and bare npm specifier handling.
Layer list, neutral-port dependency rule, outer-ring SDK adapter placement including infrastructure directories, and unlayered entrypoint wiring are all retained.
Component placement bullet preserves frontend and backend layer assignments and shared cross-cutting concerns.
Canonical text retains all allowed layers; the rule-specific notGeneric entry retains each layer's method examples, consumed inputs, produced outputs, and absence of an assembly profile.

audit.summary: All eight variants are covered by canonical text or the correctly attributed notGeneric profile. No knowledge is lost.
